newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African snub sinks hopes of Taiwan petchems deal.
newsitem.headline: S.African snub sinks hopes of Taiwan petchems deal.

text.p: Hopes of major Taiwanese investment in a petrochemical project in South Africa suffered a severe setback on Wednesday as President Nelson Mandela announced his government was ditching its old ally for Beijing.
"Certainly I would think the Taiwanese wouldn't be interested any more," said one industry observer who asked not be identified.

Officials at the Department of Trade and Industry and the Central Energy Fund, who have been handling negotiations with Taipei on the proposed scheme, said they were unaware of the latest diplomatic developments and could not comment.
Mandela announced South Africa was dropping recognition of Taiwan in favour of Beijing in a gradual process he hoped could be completed within a year.
"A permanent continuation of diplomatic recognition of the Republic of China on (the island of) Taiwan is inconsistent with South Africa's role in international affairs," Mandela said.
Taiwanese vice premier Hsu Li-teh first proposed a $3.5 billion petrochemicals complex joint venture in South Africa's Eastern Cape province during an official visit in August.
The scheme, as mooted, would entail a 50-50 joint venture integrated plant with the domestic petrochemical industry.
Several South African companies have been mentioned as potential consortium partners, including Polifin, Sasol, Sentrachem and AECI.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment.
Pretoria, whose white minority government had been a close ally of Taiwan while they were both shunned by international diplomacy, was the biggest of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies.
Taiwan has major investments in South Africa but Pretoria has also been keen to improve trade links with mainland China.
